topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic serves as the lecture's opening framing, outlining the speaker's background and the goals of the session.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: genetic mutations, environmental risks, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts of cancer development by exploring the interplay between intrinsic genetic errors, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological variation.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological agents such as viruses and bacteria drive malignancy, focusing on the discovery and mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens, metabolic activation, and DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how radiation and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic transformation to generate reactive compounds and direct DNA adducts.

topics.label: Tumor promotion and non-mutagenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the distinction between cancer initiation and promotion, demonstrating how non-mutagenic stimuli like chronic inflammation and signaling agonists stimulate clonal expansion.

topics.label: Host susceptibility factors and summary of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how host developmental timing influences vulnerability to mutagens and synthesize the core mechanisms of DNA damage and carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methods for determining carcinogenicity and evaluating risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the experimental, genomic, and epidemiological methodologies used to prove carcinogenicity and consider the practical balance of risk versus benefit.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the final concluding remarks and signoff for the lecture.
